confirmed: Source version, title and author are correct: the 14-page PDF identifies itself as the accepted, not fully edited author version in IEEE Access, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2024.3382194, by Se Jin Kim (p. 1 and repeated page headers). The entire markdown was read, including references and the end tables on pp. 13-14; no separate appendix or supplement is identified.

One original workshop study is described, combining artifact evaluation and interviews. Participants were divided into Group A without image-generative AI and Group B with Midjourney; the allocation method and randomization are not stated anywhere in the document. Retaining a provisional quasi_people design with assignment.randomized = not_stated is appropriate; has_randomized_people_study = false means not documented, not proof that assignment could not have been random (pp. 3-4, III.A-C).

The reported research sample consists of ten people, five per group, selected by purposive snowball sampling. These are students, not ideas, texts or expert ratings; the sample is below 50, n_randomized is unreported, and Table III gives no separate analyzed N (p. 4, III.C; p. 14, Table III).

The population description is supported: fashion students with three to four years of university study, seven women and three men; six aged 22-23, two aged 24 and two aged 26. The paper does not explicitly state the participants' country, so the author's South Korean affiliation should not be used to fill it (p. 4, III.C; p. 1, affiliation).

The workshop comprised three 40-minute sessions totaling 120 minutes, on the theme fun, producing a mood map, fashion style map and sketch; Group B received an additional 20-minute platform explanation (pp. 3-4, III.B).

Output-scoring eligibility is met: three fashion-design experts with doctoral degrees and more than three years of teaching experience evaluated creations on a 7-point Likert scale, using CAT criteria for mood maps and CPAM criteria for style maps and drawings (p. 4, III.D).
S1-O1 reported values match exactly: Session 1 OR, A avr 4.6 and sd 1.1; B avr 4.9 and sd 0.9; A-B avr -0.3 and sd 0.2 (p. 14, Table III).

S1-O2 reported values match exactly: Session 2 OR, A avr 4.1 and sd 1.4; B avr 5.1 and sd 0.8; A-B avr -1.0 and sd 0.6. Session 2 NE, A avr 4.0 and sd 1.4; B avr 4.9 and sd 0.9; A-B avr -0.9 (p. 14, Table III).

S1-O3 reported values match exactly: Session 3 OR, A avr 3.9 and sd 1.5; B avr 5.4 and sd 1.0; A-B avr -1.5 and sd 0.5. Session 3 NE, A avr 3.7 and sd 1.4; B avr 5.1 and sd 1.2; A-B avr -1.4. The quoted sentence about originality and newness also matches the prose (p. 14, Table III; p. 8, IV.C).

The one-line finding is numerically correct and descriptive: Group B has higher originality averages in all sessions, with Session 3 originality 5.4 versus 3.9 and newness 5.1 versus 3.7. Table III prints group averages, SDs and A-B rows, but no sample sizes, test statistics, p values or intervals; the A-B sd entries are not reported standard errors (p. 14, Table III; rating scale and participant pool on p. 4).

Sketching used pencil and paper in both groups, while previously generated AI images assisted Group B's ideation. The manuscript does not establish a later unassisted test following explicit removal of AI assistance (p. 7, IV.B.2 S3; p. 8, continuation of IV.B.2 and IV.C).
This is not a synthesis; no pooled estimates or meta-analytic study counts require extraction. Empty synthesis defaults are appropriate (pp. 3-4, III; pp. 8-9, V).

The paper states that the research had no commercial or financial support and declares no potential conflict of interest; no data or code repository is supplied (p. 1, funding statement; p. 9, Acknowledgment).
summary: The accepted manuscript describes ten students split between Midjourney and no-AI groups, with no reported random assignment, so no randomized people study is confirmed. All recorded Table III numbers and the one-line finding match, but context classification, unconfirmed analysis counts and units, unfinished outcome fields, and omitted outcomes need correction.
